headline: Expiry squeeze lifts WTI to $103.66 as Brent dips; French debt sold on riots, US yields rebound
summary: A split day in oil: expiring November WTI jumped 2.2% while Brent slipped on the Russia sanctions waiver, and gasoline fell 1.4%. Treasuries gave back their Asian gains as tech stocks rallied, leaving the 10-year near 5.13% and gold stuck under $4,200. In Europe, weekend riots pushed French yields up and the OAT–Bund spread back to about 145bp.
drivers: Oil: Hormuz beats the Russia waiver

Brent fell as low as $107.57 in Asia on Trump's Graham Act waiver, then settled at $109.55 (-0.3%) as another tanker hit a mine near Hormuz and Gulf exports held near 8.5M b/d. Expiring November WTI settled up $2.25 at $103.66 as refiners bid for domestic barrels.
French riots revive the fiscal premium

After weekend protests with more than 2,000 arrests, the 10-year OAT rose about 4–8bp to near 4.9% and the spread over Bunds widened to about 145bp, a two-week high, a day before the first 2027 budget vote.
Bonds hand back gains to stocks
The US 10-year dipped to 5.065% in Asia on lower oil and talk of smaller long-bond sales at the Nov 4 refunding, then ended about 4bp higher near 5.13% as the Nasdaq rose 1.1% on an AI rebound.
Fed on hold, December still in play
Futures price only about a 15% chance of an October hike but around 90% for one by December, which keeps real yields high and gold capped below $4,200 ahead of the Oct 27–28 meeting.

oil.note: Expiring Nov WTI settled +$2.25 (+2.2%) at $103.66; Brent Dec dipped 0.3% to $109.55.
oil.why: Brent dropped to $107.57 in Asia after Trump waived Graham Act sanctions on Russia and Rubio set a 60-day review, but the dip was bought: a tanker hit a mine near Hormuz on Sunday and Gulf crude exports are near 8.5M b/d, under half normal. WTI rallied 2.2% as refiners chased US barrels into Tuesday's November expiry, with the front spread near $2.80 in backwardation.
oil.outlook: Bias stays firm, with Brent in a $103–113 range: the waiver adds diesel at the margin but does nothing for Hormuz. Only a credible ceasefire or reopening of the strait would break $103; a weekly close above $110 opens the May highs.
oil.watch: November WTI expiry Tue Oct 20, EIA stocks Wed Oct 21, Hormuz incidents and OPEC+ on Nov 1.

gas.note: RBOB Nov settled down 4.4¢ (-1.4%) at $3.1914, down 7% this month; pump average near $4.30.
gas.why: Gasoline lagged crude because the Russia waiver and diesel deal point to more refined-product supply, and US gasoline stocks have risen for two straight weeks, including a 3.5M-barrel build to Oct 9. Seasonal demand is fading and the switch to cheaper winter blends is under way, so the crack spread is narrowing even as WTI rises.
gas.outlook: Range $3.10–3.35 a gallon with a soft bias as the crack compresses; crude above $100 limits the downside. A third straight stock build would test $3.10, while a renewed Gulf flare-up would lift it back toward $3.35.
gas.watch: EIA gasoline stocks and refinery runs Wed Oct 21, the pump average vs $4.30, and midterm fuel-price moves.

gold.note: Rejected at $4,200 again; spot near $4,140 (-0.6%), December futures about $4,160.
gold.why: Gold rose to about $4,190 in Asia as lower oil eased inflation worries, but it failed at $4,200 for the third time in two weeks once the 10-year yield climbed from 5.065% to about 5.13% and the dollar index firmed to near 102. With roughly 90% odds of a December Fed hike, a non-yielding metal struggles against 5%-plus Treasuries even with record ETF holdings.
gold.outlook: Range $4,075–4,220 into the Fed, with a slight downside tilt while the 10-year stays above 5%. A 10-year back below 5% would open a break above $4,220; a hawkish Fed or yields above 5.20% would put the $4,073 low at risk.
gold.watch: US 10-year yield and dollar, the Fed on Oct 28, then PCE inflation.

silver.note: Comex settled near $56.97, flat on the day after an early push to about $58; ratio near 72–73.
silver.why: Silver outperformed early as China's 4.5% third-quarter GDP beat and the tech rebound helped industrial metals, taking it near $58 and the gold/silver ratio down toward 72. It gave the gains back in New York as yields and the dollar rose, and settled just 2 cents lower at $56.97, close to this month's $55.55 low.
silver.outlook: Fragile while below $60, the level it lost after last week's hot CPI. Holding $56.30 keeps a bounce toward $58.50 in play; a break below $55.50 would expose the July lows near $55.
silver.watch: Equity risk appetite, Chinese demand, yields and the Fed on Oct 28.

us2y.note: Near 4.77%, up about 1–2bp; October hike odds stay around 15%.
us2y.why: The 2-year barely moved because Fed pricing is settled for now: futures give about a 15% chance of a hike on Oct 28 after Chair Warsh signalled no urgency last week, but around 90% for one by December. Lower oil early helped, but the move faded as risk assets rallied.
us2y.outlook: Pinned in a 4.70–4.80% range until the meeting. A hot PCE print or hawkish guidance would push it back toward 4.85%; a dovish hold would test 4.70%.
us2y.watch: The Fed's Oct 27–28 decision and statement, then PCE.

us5y.note: About 4.93%, up roughly 3bp after a dip in Asia.
us5y.why: The 5-year followed the long end: it fell early as oil dipped, then rose about 3bp as a 1.1% Nasdaq rebound pulled money out of the haven trade that drove Treasuries' best week since February. With CPI at 3.7%, buyers are cautious near 4.90%.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.85–5.05%. Fed guidance on a December hike matters most; a clear signal would lift the belly first.
us5y.watch: Oil, risk sentiment and the Oct 28 Fed.

us10y.note: Up about 4bp to near 5.13%, reversing a dip to 5.065% in Asia; still below last week's 5.33%.
us10y.why: The 10-year started lower on weaker oil and talk that Treasury may trim long-dated issuance at the Nov 4 refunding, after dealers were surveyed. In New York it rose to about 5.13–5.14% as AI shares rebounded and money left bonds, while WTI's late rally to $103 kept inflation concerns alive. Dow Jones put the close at 5.135%, up 3.8bp, its largest gain since Oct 2.
us10y.outlook: Range 5.00–5.30%. Talk of lighter long-bond supply and fading October hike odds cap it, but 3.7% inflation and $100 oil keep it above 5%. A close above 5.33% would restart the selloff; below 5.00% needs oil to break.
us10y.watch: Refunding signals ahead of Nov 4, oil, big tech earnings this week and the Oct 28 Fed.

us30y.note: About 5.44%, up roughly 2bp; supply hopes keep the long end steadier than the belly.
us30y.why: The 30-year rose less than shorter maturities because talk of smaller long-bond auctions at the Nov 4 refunding supports the long end. It still drifted up with the 10-year as stocks rallied and oil firmed late in the day.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.35–5.55%. Confirmation of smaller long-bond sizes would flatten the curve; no change at the refunding would add term premium back.

de2y.note: About 3.09%, up about 1bp; a December ECB hike is still mostly priced.
de2y.why: The 2-year Schatz edged up as markets kept pricing an ECB on hold on Oct 29 with a December hike largely expected; euro-area inflation is running at 3.8% and the deposit rate is 2.50%. French unrest sent some money into German paper, which limited the rise.
de2y.outlook: Range 3.00–3.15%. ECB guidance on Oct 29 decides it; a clear December signal would lift it toward 3.15%.
de2y.watch: ECB decision Oct 29 and flash October inflation.

de5y.note: About 3.23%, up about 1bp; steady while France sold off.
de5y.why: The 5-year Bund was almost unchanged because haven buying linked to France's riots offset the rise in US yields and firmer oil. Germany is trading as the safe side of eurozone stress.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.15–3.35% into the ECB. More French stress keeps it pinned; a calmer France and a hawkish ECB would push it higher.
de5y.watch: ECB Oct 29 and the OAT–Bund spread.

de10y.note: About 3.46%, up about 1–2bp; still well below the late-September high near 3.65%.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund barely moved, with wire quotes ranging from flat to up 1bp depending on the benchmark. Haven demand from French unrest balanced a rise of about 4bp in US 10-year yields, leaving the Treasury–Bund gap near 170bp.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.35–3.65%. Germany benefits from French stress; a break above 3.55% would need a hawkish ECB or a bigger global bond selloff.
de10y.watch: ECB Oct 29, German supply and US yields.

de30y.note: About 3.83%, up roughly 3bp; long end tracked global term premium.
de30y.why: The 30-year Bund rose more than shorter Bunds as long-end yields worldwide firmed in the afternoon with the US. Pension demand and haven flows from France capped the move.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.75–3.95%. It follows US long bonds more than the ECB.
de30y.watch: US long-end yields and German long-dated auctions.

fr2y.note: About 3.64%, up about 2bp; short-dated OATs least affected by the unrest.
fr2y.why: The 2-year OAT rose about 2bp, much less than the long end, because short-dated paper is tied to ECB pricing and less exposed to France's long-run fiscal path. Investors are instead charging more to hold French debt for longer.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.55–3.70%, tracking the ECB; it would jump only if a censure motion brought down the government.
fr2y.watch: Tuesday's budget vote and the ECB on Oct 29.

fr5y.note: About 4.30%, up about 3–4bp on renewed political risk.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT sold off as weekend riots, with more than 2,000 arrests, raised doubts that Prime Minister Lecornu's minority government can pass deficit cuts. The 2027 plan targets a deficit of 5.0% of GDP, and France has missed its targets in three of the last four years.
fr5y.outlook: Bias higher while the budget is in doubt; range 4.20–4.40%. A clean first-reading vote would ease pressure.
fr5y.watch: National Assembly budget vote Tue Oct 20 and any censure motion.

fr10y.note: Up about 4–8bp to near 4.9%; OAT–Bund spread about 145bp, a two-week high.
fr10y.why: France's 10-year yield jumped as much as 8–10bp after the weekend's worst unrest in years over living costs and public services, a day before the first 2027 budget vote. The spread over Bunds widened to about 145bp, near euro-crisis levels though below the near-160bp peak of early October, and French yields now sit above Italy's and Greece's.
fr10y.outlook: Spread bias wider, in a 135–160bp range, since investors doubt real fiscal consolidation with a 2027 presidential race ahead. The ECB is unlikely to step in unless trading becomes disorderly; a failed vote or censure motion would take the 10-year back toward 5%.
fr10y.watch: Budget vote Tue Oct 20, further protests, and rating reviews.

fr30y.note: Up about 6bp to near 5.49%; the long end carries the biggest fiscal premium.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT rose the most on the curve, about 6bp, as investors demanded more compensation to hold French debt for decades amid street violence and doubts over a 2027 budget that projects about €91 billion in interest costs.
fr30y.outlook: The most exposed part of the curve: it will move most if the budget stalls or ratings are cut. A break above 5.55% would retest this month's highs.
fr30y.watch: The budget vote and long-dated OAT auctions.

watch: Next: Tuesday's WTI November expiry and French budget vote, EIA stocks on Wednesday, big tech earnings, the Fed on Oct 27–28, the ECB on Oct 29, OPEC+ on Nov 1 and the Nov 4 US refunding.
